test_title: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 18 Jul 2023 Shift 4)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following pairs is/are correctly matched regarding the terminology used in the Parliament?

A. Appropriation Bill - A Money Bill passed for providing for the withdrawal or appropriation from and out of the Consolidated Fund of India

B. Demand for Grants - Earmarking of budgetary allocation for meeting only planned expenditure of a Ministry/Department

C. Short Duration Discussion - For raising a discussion on a matter of urgent public importance for which a notice has to be given by a Member and supported by 50 Members
solution:
The correct answer is __**A only**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A. Appropriation Bill - The Appropriation Bill is indeed a Money Bill passed for providing for the withdrawal or appropriation from and out of the Consolidated Fund of India. Therefore, this option is correctly matched.
 
• B. Demand for Grants and C. Short Duration Discussion - are incorrectly paired in the context provided.
 
 
• The "Demands for Grants" are the estimates of expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India, presented to the Lok Sabha for its approval. The demands are presented ministry-wise.
 
• A "Short Duration Discussion" in the Indian parliament refers to a discussion on a matter of urgent public importance, which can be raised with prior notice, but it does not need to be supported by 50 members, so again the pairing is incorrect.
 
 
 
• So, based on the given pairs, the correct answer is "A only".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Money Bill**: Any bill that pertains to taxation and government finances is classified as a Money Bill under Article 110. The Speaker of the Lok Sabha holds the authority to decide whether a financial bill is a Money Bill or not. In the case of Money Bills, the Rajya Sabha (Upper House) has limited powers—all amendments recommended by Rajya Sabha are not binding on Lok Sabha.
 
• **Ordinance**: Under Article 123, the President of India is empowered to issue ordinances when Parliament is not in session, and immediate legislative action is needed. However, such an ordinance must be approved by the Parliament within six weeks of its next session.
 
• **Question Hour**: This is the first hour of a parliamentary sitting/session where Members of Parliament ask questions to ministers and hold them accountable for the functioning of their ministries.
 
• **Zero Hour**: Unlike the Question Hour, the Zero Hour is not mentioned in any rules of procedure. Thus, it is an informal but powerful tool available to the members of the Parliament to raise matters of great importance without any prior notice.
 
• **Quorum (Article 100)**: This refers to the minimum number of Members of Parliament that must be present to make the proceedings of that House valid. In India, the quorum to conduct a meeting of either House of Parliament is one-tenth of the total number of seats in that House.
 
• **Powers, Privileges, etc. of Parliament Members (Article 105)**: According to this article, the Parliament and its members and committees have powers and privileges that are necessary for the exercise of their responsibilities. No Member of Parliament can be held liable in any court for anything that is said, or any vote given, in Parliament or its committee meetings.
 
• **Motion of No Confidence**: This is a statement or vote that states or proposes that a government must be called into account. A motion of no confidence mandates the government to prove its majority in the house.
 
• **Private Member's Bill**: Any bill introduced by a Member of Parliament who is not a minister is called a private member's bill. These bills are treated the same as other public bills, but in practicality, they have little chance of being passed due to lower precedence on the legislative agenda.
 
• **Cut Motions**: These are objections raised in Lok Sabha to the demand made for grants, essentially objections to the amount of financial expenditure.
